The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a compact, connected, oriented, boundaryless smooth manifold of dimension $d\in\{3,4\}$ with a smooth Riemannian metric, let $N\ge2$, and fix a smooth right principal $SU(N)$-bundle $\pi:P\to M$, a smooth connection $A_0$, and a point $p_m\in P$ over $x_m\in M$. Use the standard unitary representation of $SU(N)$ on $\mathbb C^N$ and the invariant positive inner product $\langle X,Y\rangle=-\operatorname{tr}(XY)$ on $\mathfrak{su}(N)$. Define the adjoint vector bundle $\operatorname{ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}\mathfrak{su}(N)$ and the adjoint group bundle $\operatorname{Ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}SU(N)$ with associated-bundle relation $[pg,z]=[p,\operatorname{Ad}_g z]$.

Choose one finite smooth bundle atlas with relatively compact coordinate domains and a subordinate partition of unity. For each integer $k>d/2+1$, let $H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$ be the Sobolev completions of smooth sections in the resulting finite-atlas norms. Define the affine configuration space $\mathcal A_k:=A_0+H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and the set $\mathcal G_{k+1}:=H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ of Sobolev gauge sections. The next lemma proves that the pointwise product and inverse close on this set and make it a Hilbert Lie group. Its based subset is $\mathcal G_{k+1,m}:=\{u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}:u(p_m)=e\}$. Let $Z_N=\{zI_N:z^N=1\}$ be the center of $SU(N)$, viewed as constant gauge sections. Indeed, if $Z=(z_{ij})$ is central and $D=\operatorname{diag}(t_1,\ldots,t_N)\in SU(N)$, then $(t_j-t_i)z_{ij}=0$. For each $i\ne j$ one can choose such a diagonal matrix with $t_i\ne t_j$, so $Z$ is diagonal. Commuting with the determinant-one unitary rotation whose block on the $(i,j)$ coordinates is $\begin{pmatrix}\cos t&\sin t\\-\sin t&\cos t\end{pmatrix}$ for $t\notin\pi\mathbb Z$ forces the $i$th and $j$th diagonal entries equal. Hence $Z=zI_N$; determinant one gives $z^N=1$, and conversely every such scalar is central. Write $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}$ for the set of $Z_N$-cosets with quotient topology; the next lemma also verifies that the induced pointwise operation makes it a Hilbert Lie group.

Let $\mathcal A_\infty:=A_0+\Omega^1(M,\operatorname{ad}P)$ and let $\mathcal G_\infty$ be the smooth gauge group, with the $C^\infty$ section topology generated by all finite-atlas derivative seminorms. Define $\bar{\mathcal G}_\infty:=\mathcal G_\infty/Z_N$. In a local section of $P$, write a connection as a matrix-valued one-form $A$ and a gauge section as a map $u$ into $SU(N)$; the right gauge action is $A^u:=u^{-1}Au+u^{-1}du$, equivalently pullback by the gauge automorphism associated with $u$. The calculus lemma proves that this formula defines a smooth action on the Sobolev spaces above. For an adjoint section $\xi$, set $d_A\xi:=d\xi+[A,\xi]$ using the degree-one Lie-algebra-valued-form bracket. In local coordinates and an orthonormal adjoint frame, define the formal adjoint on an adjoint-valued one-form $a$ by $(d_A^*a)=-g^{ij}(\nabla_i^{\mathrm{LC}}a_j+[A_i,a_j])$, where $\nabla^{\mathrm{LC}}$ differentiates the covector index. This is the $L^2$ adjoint for the Riemannian volume and stated fiber metric; its local coefficient formula defines a distribution at Sobolev regularity.

For $A\in\mathcal A_k$, parallel transport of its $C^1$ connection form around piecewise smooth loops based at $p_m$ defines a subgroup $\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A)\subseteq SU(N)$. Call $A$ irreducible when this subgroup leaves no nonzero proper complex subspace of $\mathbb C^N$ invariant; changing the chosen frame conjugates the subgroup and leaves this condition unchanged. Write $\mathcal A_k^*$ and $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ for the irreducible loci. Once the calculus lemma verifies the group action, define orbit equivalence by $A\sim B$ exactly when $B=A^u$ for some gauge section $u$; all resulting quotients carry the quotient topology, whose open sets are those with open inverse image under the orbit projection.

Assume the configuration data and integer $k>d/2+1$ from the preceding definition, and let $\mathcal A_k^*$ be the locus where the holonomy representation on $\mathbb C^N$ is irreducible. For any $A\in\mathcal A_k$, evaluation at $p_m$ identifies its stabilizer in $\mathcal G_{k+1}$ with the centralizer of $\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A)$ in $SU(N)$. Thus an irreducible connection has stabilizer exactly $Z_N$, and the induced action of $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}=\mathcal G_{k+1}/Z_N$ on $\mathcal A_k^*$ is free. The subset $\mathcal A_k^*$ is open in $\mathcal A_k$.

The Sobolev action is proper: if $A_j\to A$ and $A_j^{u_j}\to B$ in $H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ for sequences $A_j,A,B\in\mathcal A_k$ and $u_j\in\mathcal G_{k+1}$, then some subsequence $u_{j_\ell}$ converges in $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ to $u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}$ and $B=A^u$. Equivalently, the action map $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}\times\mathcal A_k^*\to\mathcal A_k^*\times\mathcal A_k^*$ is proper, meaning inverse images of compact sets are compact.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M,E,P$ have exactly the compact, boundaryless, scalar-positive-symbol and formal symmetry hypotheses of [[thm-elliptic-differential-operators-on-compact-vector-bundles-have-parametrices-and-regularity]], with $\operatorname{dom}P=H^2(M,E)$. Write $\mathcal H=\ker P$.

Then $\mathcal H$ is finite dimensional and consists of smooth sections, $\operatorname{ran}P=\mathcal H^\perp$ is closed in $L^2$, and
$$L^2(M,E)=\mathcal H\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}\operatorname{ran}P.$$
Let $\Pi$ be the orthogonal projection onto $\mathcal H$. There is a unique linear operator $G:L^2\to H^2\cap\mathcal H^\perp$ with
$$PG=I-\Pi\quad\hbox{on }L^2,\qquad GP=I-\Pi\quad\hbox{on }H^2,\qquad G\Pi=\Pi G=0.$$
It is bounded from $H^k$ to $H^{k+2}$ for every integer $k\ge0$, compact and selfadjoint on $L^2$, and preserves smooth sections. For all such $k$,
$$H^k=\mathcal H\oplus P(H^{k+2}),\qquad C^\infty(M,E)=\mathcal H\oplus P(C^\infty(M,E)),$$
where the second summands are the corresponding intersections with $\mathcal H^\perp$, and the decompositions are topological. The projection is smoothing: for every integer $r\ge0$, $\|\Pi f\|_{C^r}\le C_r\|f\|_2$. Consequently $G$ is a two-sided parametrix with finite-rank smoothing remainders. If additionally $(Pu,u)_2\ge0$ for smooth $u$, then $P$ and $G$ are nonnegative on their respective domains.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold without boundary of real dimension $n\ge2$, equipped with a smooth positive density, and $E\to M$ a finite-rank real Euclidean or complex Hermitian smooth vector bundle. Let $P$ be a smooth-coefficient second-order differential operator on $E$, formally symmetric for the density and metric, whose positive-frequency principal symbol is
$$\sigma_2(P)(x,\xi)=a_x(\xi,\xi)I_{E_x},$$
where $a$ is a smooth positive-definite real quadratic form on cotangent vectors. Thus in any local frame $P=-a^{ij}\partial_i\partial_j+B^j\partial_j+C$, with scalar real positive-definite $a^{ij}$ and matrix-valued lower coefficients. Nonnegativity of $P$ is not needed here.

For nonnegative integers $k$, define $H^k(M,E)$ by requiring the coefficients of each member of a finite smooth partition of unity times the section, in precompact bundle charts and extended by zero, to lie in $H^k(\mathbb R^n)$; the norm is the square root of the sum of these component Sobolev norms squared. Different such choices give equivalent norms. The following hold.

1. These are Hilbert spaces, smooth sections are dense, $H^0=L^2$ with equivalent norms, $H^{k+1}\hookrightarrow H^k$ is compact, and $H^k\hookrightarrow C^r$ continuously whenever $k>r+n/2$.
2. If $u\in H^1$ and $Pu=f\in H^k$ distributionally, then $u\in H^{k+2}$ and
$$\|u\|_{H^{k+2}}\le C_k(\|f\|_{H^k}+\|u\|_{L^2}).$$
In particular smooth data give smooth weak solutions. The same estimate holds for all $u\in H^{k+2}$.
3. For sufficiently large real $\lambda>0$, $P+\lambda:H^2\to L^2$ is a bounded bijection with bounded inverse $B:L^2\to H^2$. As an operator on $L^2$, $B$ is compact, injective and selfadjoint, has dense range $H^2$, and the unbounded operator $P$ with domain exactly $H^2$ is selfadjoint. The map $B:H^k\to H^{k+2}$ is bounded for every nonnegative integer $k$ and preserves smooth sections.
4. It supplies two-sided parametrices **modulo compact operators**:
$$PB=I-\lambda B\quad\hbox{on }L^2,\qquad BP=I-\lambda B\quad\hbox{on }H^2.$$
Here on the second space $B$ denotes its restriction after inclusion $H^2\hookrightarrow L^2$; it is compact on $H^2$. No assertion concerning arbitrary-order elliptic operators, or pseudodifferential symbol classes, is part of this theorem.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let $m\ge1$. For every
$\varepsilon>0$ there is $C=C(n,m,\varepsilon)$ such that every
$u\in H^{m+1}_0(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ satisfies
$$\|D^mu\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le\varepsilon\,\|D^{m+1}u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}+C\,\|D^{m-1}u\|_{L^2(\Omega)},$$
and the same estimate holds for every $u\in H^{m+1}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ whose
class vanishes almost everywhere outside a compact subset of $\Omega$. In
both displays
$$\|D^ju\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2:=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n,\,|\alpha|=j}\|D^\alpha u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2 .$$
In particular, for $u\in H^2_0(\Omega;\mathbb K)$,
$$\|Du\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le\varepsilon\|D^2u\|_{L^2(\Omega)}+C_\varepsilon\|u\|_{L^2(\Omega)} .$$
The constants are not asserted sharp, and the estimate is the tool that
absorbs commutator terms linear in the highest derivatives.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ and $Y$ be Banach
spaces over the same scalar field, let $T:X\to Y$ be a Fredholm operator and let
$K:X\to Y$ be compact ([[def-fredholm-operator-cokernel-and-index]],
[[def-compact-linear-operator]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). Then $T+K$
is Fredholm and $\operatorname{ind}(T+K)=\operatorname{ind}T$.

Let $X$ and $Y$ be Banach spaces over the same scalar field
([[def-banach-space]]).

1. If $R\in\mathcal B(X)$ satisfies $\|R\|<1$
   ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]), then $I-R$ is
   invertible with inverse the operator-norm limit of the partial sums
   $\sum_{n<N}R^n$, the norm limit being taken in
   $\mathcal B(X)$ ([[def-space-of-bounded-linear-operators]]), and
   $$\Bigl\|\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}R^n\Bigr\|\le\frac{1}{1-\|R\|}.$$
2. If $A\in\mathcal B(X,Y)$ is invertible with $A^{-1}\in\mathcal B(Y,X)$ and
   $E\in\mathcal B(X,Y)$ satisfies $\|A^{-1}E\|<1$, then $A+E$ is invertible
   with $(A+E)^{-1}=\bigl(I+A^{-1}E\bigr)^{-1}A^{-1}\in\mathcal B(Y,X)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega$ be a bounded $W^{k,p}$-extension domain, $k\ge1$ and $1\le p<\infty$ with $kp>n$. Then there is $C(n,p,k,\Omega)$ with
$$\|uv\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}\|v\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}\qquad(u,v\in W^{k,p}(\Omega)),$$
so $W^{k,p}(\Omega)$ is a Banach algebra; the constants and the conclusion may depend on the choice of equivalent Sobolev norm only through $C$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega$ be a bounded $W^{k,p}$-extension domain, $k\ge1$ and $1\le p<\infty$. Let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ and $u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Then:

1. if $kp<n$, $\|u\|_{L^q(\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ for every $q$ with $\frac1q\ge\frac1p-\frac kn$ (equivalently $1\le q\le\frac{np}{n-kp}$);
2. if $kp=n$, $\|u\|_{L^q(\Omega)}\le C(q)\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ for every finite $q$;
3. if $kp>n$, then for every integer $m\ge0$ and every $0<\alpha<1$ with $m+\alpha<k-\frac np$ there is a representative in $C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ with $\|u\|_{C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$; when $k-\frac np\notin\mathbb Z$ one may take $m=\lfloor k-\frac np\rfloor$ and $\alpha=k-\frac np-m$.

Here $C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ uses the continuous derivatives of the constructed representative on an ambient neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega$, with norm
$$\|g\|_{C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}:=\sum_{|\beta|\le m}\sup_{\overline\Omega}|D^\beta g|+\sum_{|\beta|=m}\sup_{\substack{x,y\in\overline\Omega\\x\ne y}}\frac{|D^\beta g(x)-D^\beta g(y)|}{|x-y|^\alpha}.$$
For $\Omega=\varnothing$ set these norm values to $0$. The proof supplies such an ambient representative, so no boundary differentiability or regularity of $\partial\Omega$ is assumed.

Assume the configuration data of the preceding definition. For every integer $k>d/2+1$, all finite-atlas Sobolev norms on the specified section and form spaces are equivalent, $H^k$ embeds continuously in $C^1$, and pointwise multiplication of matrix or adjoint-bundle $H^k$ sections is bounded. The set $\mathcal G_{k+1}=H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ is a Hilbert Lie group modeled on $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$, and the right gauge action $\mathcal A_k\times\mathcal G_{k+1}\to\mathcal A_k$ is smooth. At $(A,e)$ its differential, in the affine and exponential coordinates, is

$$D\bigl((A+a)^{\exp\xi}\bigr)_{(0,0)}(a,\xi)=a+d_A\xi,$$

where $a\in H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and $\xi\in H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$.

Fix the smooth reference connection $A_0$ from the configuration data and set $h=A-A_0\in H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$. In a local orthonormal frame, $d_A=d_{A_0}+[h,\cdot]$ on zero-forms and $d_A^*=d_{A_0}^*-\iota_h$ on one-forms, where $\iota_h(a)=g^{ij}[h_i,a_j]$. Therefore $K_A:=\Delta_A-\Delta_{A_0}$ is a finite sum of terms of the forms $(
abla_{A_0}h)\xi$, $h
abla_{A_0}\xi$, and $h^2\xi$. These terms define a bounded map $H^{k+1}	o H^{k-1}$. They are compact: $(
abla_{A_0}h)\xi$ factors through the compact inclusion $H^{k+1}\hookrightarrow H^{k-1}$ followed by multiplication in the algebra $H^{k-1}$; $h
abla_{A_0}\xi$ and $h^2\xi$ first map boundedly into $H^k$ and then use the compact inclusion $H^k\hookrightarrow H^{k-1}$. Here $k-1>d/2$, so the needed multiplication bounds follow from [F8].

Apply [F3] with $r=k-1\ge0$ to $\Delta_{A_0}:H^{k+1}\to H^{k-1}$. Its kernel is finite dimensional, and the Hodge theorem gives the topological direct decomposition $H^{k-1}=\ker\Delta_{A_0}\oplus\Delta_{A_0}(H^{k+1})$. Thus its range is closed with codimension equal to the kernel dimension, so $\Delta_{A_0}$ is Fredholm of index zero. By [F6] and the compactness of $K_A$ from step 1.1, $\Delta_A=\Delta_{A_0}+K_A$ is Fredholm of index zero.

The smooth reference estimate [F4] and $\Delta_{A_0}=\Delta_A-K_A$ give $\|\xi\|_{H^{k+1}}\le C(\|\Delta_A\xi\|_{H^{k-1}}+\|K_A\xi\|_{H^{k-1}}+\|\xi\|_{L^2})$. The three terms in $K_A$ from step 1.1 satisfy $\|K_A\xi\|_{H^{k-1}}\le C_A\|\xi\|_{H^k}$. The Sobolev interpolation estimate $\|\xi\|_{H^k}\le\varepsilon\|\xi\|_{H^{k+1}}+C_\varepsilon\|\xi\|_{L^2}$ follows by finite-atlas localization and the estimate in [F5]. Choose $\varepsilon$ so that the resulting $H^{k+1}$ term is absorbed into the left side. This yields $\|\xi\|_{H^{k+1}}\le C_A'(\|\Delta_A\xi\|_{H^{k-1}}+\|\xi\|_{L^2})$.

If $\Delta_A\xi=0$ for $\xi\in H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$, the formal-adjoint identity, first for smooth approximants and then by Sobolev continuity, gives $0=\langle\Delta_A\xi,\xi\rangle_{L^2}=\|d_A\xi\|_{L^2}^2$. Hence $d_A\xi=0$. Parallel transport makes $\xi$ determined by $\xi(p_m)$, and that value commutes with holonomy. By [F2], $\exp(t\xi(p_m))$ lies in the finite group $Z_N$ for every real $t$, because $\xi(p_m)$ commutes with holonomy. The path is continuous and equals the identity at $t=0$, so it is constant; differentiating at zero gives $\xi(p_m)=0$. Parallel transport then gives $\xi=0$.

Since $\Delta_A$ is Fredholm of index zero and its kernel is zero by step 3.1, its cokernel has dimension zero. Its range is closed by the Fredholm property, so $\Delta_A$ is onto and therefore bijective.

If no constant bounded $\|\xi\|_{H^{k+1}}$ by $\|\Delta_A\xi\|_{H^{k-1}}$, choose $\|\xi_j\|_{H^{k+1}}=1$ with $\Delta_A\xi_j\to0$. By [F4], a subsequence converges in $L^2$; applying the estimate of step 2.2 to differences shows it is Cauchy in $H^{k+1}$. Its limit has $H^{k+1}$ norm one and lies in $\ker\Delta_A$, contradicting step 3.1. Thus $\|\xi\|_{H^{k+1}}\le C_A''\|\Delta_A\xi\|_{H^{k-1}}$. Together with bijectivity this proves the inverse $G_A$ is bounded.

The operator-valued map $A\mapsto\Delta_A\in\mathcal B(H^{k+1},H^{k-1})$ is a continuous polynomial of degree at most two in the local coefficients of $A$, by step 1.1 and the product estimates [F8]. Near a fixed irreducible $A$, write $\Delta_{A+h}=\Delta_A+E(h)$; for small $h$, [F7] gives $(\Delta_{A+h})^{-1}=(I+G_AE(h))^{-1}G_A=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(-G_AE(h))^nG_A$. On a neighborhood where $\|G_AE(h)\|\le\rho<1$, the Neumann series converges in operator norm. Its $m$-th derivative is bounded termwise by a constant times $n^m\rho^{n-m}$ for $n\ge m$, whose series converges; hence all derivatives converge uniformly on a smaller neighborhood. This proves that inversion and $A\mapsto G_A$ are smooth there.

Define $\Pi_A=d_AG_Ad_A^*$. The Sobolev orders give a bounded map $H^k(\Omega^1(\operatorname{ad}P))\to H^k(\Omega^1(\operatorname{ad}P))$. Since $\Delta_A G_A=I$ and $G_A\Delta_A=I$, one has $\Pi_A d_A\xi=d_A\xi$ and $d_A^*(I-\Pi_A)a=0$ for every $\xi\in H^{k+1}$ and $a\in H^k$. Their ranges intersect trivially: if $d_A\xi\in\ker d_A^*$, then $\Delta_A\xi=0$, so step 3.1 gives $\xi=0$. This proves the direct-sum decomposition and projection formula. Smooth dependence of $G_A$, $d_A$, and $d_A^*$ from step 5.1 makes $\Pi_A$ smooth in $A$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.

$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

$$\mathcal O(-1)\otimes_A U_A\xrightarrow{\alpha_A}\mathcal O\otimes_A S_A\xrightarrow{\beta_A}\mathcal O(1)\otimes_A U'_A,$$
where $U_A,S_A,U'_A$ are free $A$-modules of ranks $k,2k+N,k$, each map is homogeneous linear in $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)$, $\beta_A\alpha_A=0$, $\alpha_A$ is a locally split injection, $\beta_A$ is a locally split surjection, and $F_A=\ker\beta_A/\operatorname{im}\alpha_A$ is locally free of rank $N$. The two short exact sequences defined by the kernel and image split locally; hence their formation and the middle cohomology commute with reduction $A\to\mathbb C$. The reduced complex is therefore an ordinary linear monad on $\mathbb P^3_\mathbb C$.

The **first-order locally-free/base-change range** used here further requires that $H^0(\mathbb P^3_A,F_A)$ is a free $A$-module and reduction identifies it with $H^0(\mathbb P^3_\mathbb C,F_0)$, where $F_0=F_A\otimes_A\mathbb C$. The image in $S_A$ of the map from the four coefficient copies of $U_A$ under $\alpha_A$ is a direct summand and reduces to the corresponding coefficient-image subspace of $S_0$. For each real twistor line $\ell$ in the reduced projective space, the restriction of $F_A$ to $\ell_A=\ell\times_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Spec}A$ is trivial of rank $N$, and reduction identifies its global sections with $H^0(\ell,F_0|_\ell)$. These conditions state the precise global, coefficient-image, and line-section base-change range; no arbitrary analytic family or algebraization assertion is included.

Extend the coordinate map $j(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$ semilinearly using the involution of $A$; its projective action $\sigma$ is an involution and preserves each real twistor line. A **real twistor line** means the projectivization of a $j$-invariant complex two-plane in $\mathbb C^4$. Equivalently these are the finite lines
$$\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2,\qquad \mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2,\qquad (z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2,$$
together with $\ell_\infty=\{\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0\}$. Indeed a nonzero vector $v$ and $jv$ are complex-linearly independent because $j^2=-1$; they span the invariant plane. If its $\lambda$ projection is nonzero, that projection and its quaternionic conjugate give an invertible two-by-two matrix with determinant $|\lambda_1|^2+|\lambda_2|^2$, so it has exactly the displayed graph form; if the projection is zero the plane is the $\mu$ plane. Each fixed-line restriction above means the corresponding constant thickening $\ell_A$.

A first-order real structure on the monad is a nondegenerate holomorphic $\sigma$-Hermitian pairing on $F_A$, linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second, whose reduction induces a positive-definite Hermitian form on the holomorphic section space of every real line. A unitary framing at infinity is an isometric isomorphism $F_A|_{\ell_\infty}\cong (A\otimes_\mathbb C W)\otimes_A\mathcal O_{\ell_\infty}$, where $\ell_\infty=\{\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0\}$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ has its standard Hermitian form.

An isomorphism of such families is an $A$-linear chain isomorphism that intertwines the $\sigma$-Hermitian pairings and the framing. No order or positivity is assigned to elements of $A$ with nonzero nilpotent part: positivity is required only after reduction. The base-change scope in this definition consists exactly of reduction $\epsilon\mapsto0$ and the involution-preserving maps $\rho_r$ for real $r$.

Let $\mathcal F$ be the locally free algebraic middle cohomology of a linear monad
$$
\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(-1)^{\oplus k}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}^{\oplus(2k+N)}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(1)^{\oplus k}
$$
on $\mathbb P^3_\mathbb C$, with exactness at both ends. Let $H_{\rm alg}=c_1^{\rm alg}(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(1))$ in the Chow ring and let $H_{\rm top}=c_1^{\rm top}(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(1))$ in singular cohomology. The hyperplane cycle map identifies $H_{\rm alg}$ with $H_{\rm top}$; write $H$ for either class in the corresponding formula. The algebraic Chern character is $N-kH_{\rm alg}^2$, the algebraic first Chern class is zero, the algebraic second Chern class is $kH_{\rm alg}^2$, and the algebraic Euler characteristic is $N-2k$. The underlying topological bundle has total Chern class $1+kH_{\rm top}^2$ through degree six and topological Chern character $N-kH_{\rm top}^2$.

Identify $\mathbb P^3_\mathbb C$ with the twistor space of $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ by the quaternionic structure whose invariant lines are the real incidence lines in the positive stereographic coordinates. Let $\pi:\mathbb P^3_\mathbb C\to S^4$ be the resulting fibration, orient each fiber by its complex orientation, orient the base so the incidence chart followed by the fiber orientation gives the complex orientation of $\mathbb P^3$, and let $u\in H^4(S^4;\mathbb Z)$ be the positive point class. Then $\pi^*u=H^2$. Consequently, if the underlying topological bundle of $\mathcal F$ is $\pi^*E$ for a rank-$N$ complex bundle $E\to S^4$ with $c_1(E)=0$, then $c_2(E)=ku$ and $\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle=k$.

Assume AC. Fix $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, standard Hermitian $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$ and ADHM data $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with the complex equation $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. Stability means that the $B_1,B_2$ words applied to $I(W)$ span $V$; costability means no nonzero common invariant subspace of $V$ lies in $\ker J$; regular means both. Set

$$\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

For every $\zeta>0$, each stable $GL(V)$ orbit meets $\mu_{\mathbb R}=\zeta I_V$ in exactly one $U(V)$ orbit, and the inclusion induces a diffeomorphism of smooth real manifolds

$$\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}=\zeta I_V,\ \mathrm{stable}\}/U(V)\ \cong\ X^s/GL(V).$$

At $\zeta=0$, every stable datum satisfying the real equation is automatically costable. Each regular complex orbit meets the zero real level in exactly one unitary orbit, giving instead

$$\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}=0,\ \mathrm{stable}\}/U(V)\ \cong\ X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V).$$

Both identifications are equivariant for the compact rotation/framing torus in the raw-data convention. For $k=0$ all spaces are points. This theorem identifies the stated finite-dimensional quotients; it asserts no correspondence with sheaves or ASD connections, and no identification of the entire positive-FI quotient with the zero-FI regular locus.

For $r\ge1$, let $H=\{[Z_0:\cdots:Z_r]\in\mathbb P^r(\mathbb C):Z_0=0\}$ and
let $i:H\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^r(\mathbb C)$ be inclusion. For every
integer $m$, the homogeneous coordinate $Z_0$ defines an exact sequence of
holomorphic sheaves
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(m-1) \xrightarrow{\ \cdot Z_0\ }\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(m) \longrightarrow i_*\mathcal O_H(m)\longrightarrow0.$$
Here $i_*\mathcal O_H(m)$ assigns to an open set $U$ the holomorphic
sections of $\mathcal O_H(m)$ on $U\cap H$. Twisting the sequence with
$m=0$ by $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(-1)$ gives, in particular,
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(-2) \longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(-1) \longrightarrow i_*\mathcal O_H(-1)\longrightarrow0.$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a commutative
ring with $1$ ([[def-commutative-ring]]), let $n\ge0$, let $d\in\mathbb Z$ and
let $X=\mathbb P^n_A\cong\operatorname{Proj}A[x_0,\dots,x_n]$ be relative
projective space ([[def-relative-projective-space-standard-charts]],
[[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]]), with twisting sheaf
$\mathcal O_X(d)$ ([[def-twisting-sheaf-proj]]) and cohomology
$H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$. Then
$$H^q(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=0\qquad\text{unless }q=0\text{ or }q=n.$$
If $n>0$, then $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\cong A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_d$ when $d\ge0$
and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))=0$ when $d<0$, where
$A[x_0,\dots,x_n]_d$ is the degree-$d$ graded piece
([[def-graded-ring-and-graded-module]]); and $H^n(X,\mathcal O_X(d))$ is the
free $A$-module on the Laurent monomials $x_0^{e_0}\cdots x_n^{e_n}$ with
$e_i<0$ for every $i$ and $\sum_ie_i=d$, so that it is nonzero precisely when
$d\le-n-1$ and $A\ne0$. For $n=0$ one has $\mathbb P^0_A=\operatorname{Spec}A$
and $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(d))\cong A$ for every $d\in\mathbb Z$, with all higher
groups zero. The zero ring $A=0$ is allowed: then $X=\varnothing$ and all
groups are zero, in agreement with both displayed descriptions.

derivations.claim: First the holomorphic monad maps have homogeneous linear entries. Indeed, in the $m=1$ sequence of [F10], $H^1(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O)=0$ by [A1], so restriction $H^0(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O(1))\to H^0(\mathbb P^{r-1},\mathcal O(1))$ is surjective and its kernel is the defining hyperplane coordinate times $H^0(\mathcal O)=\mathbb C$. Starting with $r=0$, where $\mathcal O(1)$ on a point has one-dimensional section space, induction shows that every section is a linear combination of the homogeneous coordinates: subtract the global coordinate lifts of its restriction, then the remaining section is a constant multiple of the defining coordinate. This applies to entries of both $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O(-1),\mathcal O)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O,\mathcal O(1))$. Thus no algebraic/analytic comparison is needed to introduce their four coefficient maps. By [A1] and [F9], the hyperplane sequences and analytic scalar theorem give exactly the negative-twist vanishings required by [F1]. Apply [F1] to the pairing isomorphism; it gives the unique constant Hermitian lift $H$ with the signed identities there. Thus no algebraic cohomology group is being substituted for the analytic lifting groups.

For the algebraic $\mathbb P^3_A=\operatorname{Proj}A[\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2]$ family category, [F11] directly supplies the needed $\mathcal O(-1)$ and $\mathcal O(-2)$ groups over $A$ and $H^0(\mathcal O_A)=A$. Separately, on the analytic first-order thickening each twist has the split underlying analytic sheaf $\mathcal O_A(d)=\mathcal O(d)\oplus\epsilon\mathcal O(d)$; finite direct sums commute with sheaf cohomology, so [F9] gives the same vanishings there. Thus a holomorphic family pairing can be lifted analytically, whereas algebraic family sheaves use [F11]; neither computation substitutes algebraic cohomology for an analytic group or invokes GAGA. Both yield constant $A$-valued chain maps. In both categories the two kernel/image sequences identify global sections with the same constant coefficient kernel of $\beta_A$, so the specified global-section base-change condition is respected by this identification. Repeating the obstruction and ambiguity calculation of [F1] over these coefficient modules lifts the family pairing uniquely to an $A$-linear constant chain isomorphism with Hermitian middle matrix $H_A$; its inverse exists because its reduction is invertible. Global section base change identifies $H^0(F_A)$ with the constant coefficient kernel $L_A$ in $S_A$. Its reduction is injective, so a full-rank minor is a unit and $L_A$ is a direct summand.

By [F2], the global constant subspace $L$ is positive and $S=L\oplus M$ orthogonally, and the reduced monad on $M$ preserves the full framing. Apply [F3] to that reduced monad; it proves $H|_M$ positive. Since $H|_L$ is positive and the sum is orthogonal, $H$ is positive definite on all of $S$. In particular the argument also covers $k=0$, where $M=0$.

By hypothesis the coefficient-image module $M_A$ is a direct summand. The coefficient identities give $M_A^\perp=L_A$; for a direct summand in a finite free module with a perfect pairing, the restriction map to its dual is split-surjective, so taking orthogonal complements twice returns that summand. Hence $M_A=L_A^\perp$ and $S_A=L_A\oplus M_A$. The line-section base change and the vanishing $H^0(\ell_A,\mathcal O(-1))=0$ make restriction of $L_A$ injective; the reduced line positivity makes $H_A|_{L_0}$ positive. The internal-positivity proof applies to the reduction on $M_0$, so its reduced form is positive too. On infinity the family framing identifies the remaining orthogonal complement isometrically with $W_A$.

Write the four coefficient maps of $\alpha$ as $P=\alpha_{\lambda_1}$, $Q=\alpha_{\lambda_2}$, $R=\alpha_{\mu_1}$, and $T=\alpha_{\mu_2}$. From the first-slot convention and $j^2=-1$, the corresponding coefficients of $\beta$ are $Q^\dagger H,-P^\dagger H,T^\dagger H,-R^\dagger H$ in that order. The $\mu_1^2,\mu_2^2,\mu_1\mu_2$ coefficients of $\beta\alpha=0$ give $T^\dagger HR=R^\dagger HT=0$ and $R^\dagger HR=T^\dagger HT$. The maps $R,T$ are injective by exactness at the two coordinate points of $\ell_\infty$. Positivity of $H$ therefore makes their common Gram matrix $G$ positive definite. Replacing the paired end bases by $G^{-1/2}$ normalizes both maps to isometries with orthogonal images. Choosing an orthonormal basis of $S$ then identifies $R=-\iota_1$, $T=-\iota_2$ and $S=(V\oplus V)\oplus W_0$, with $W_0$ their orthogonal complement.

At infinity the maps are $\alpha_\infty=-\mu_1\iota_1-\mu_2\iota_2$ and $\beta_\infty=\mu_2\iota_1^\dagger-\mu_1\iota_2^\dagger$. For every $[\mu_1:\mu_2]\in\mathbb P^1$, the kernel of $\beta_\infty$ in $V\oplus V$ is the line-valued copy $\{(\mu_1v,\mu_2v):v\in V\}$, which is exactly the image of $\alpha_\infty$; $W_0$ is killed by $\beta_\infty$ and meets that image trivially. Therefore the restricted cohomology and its section pairing are canonically $W_0\otimes\mathcal O_{\ell_\infty}$ and its standard positive form. The specified unitary framing identifies $W_0$ with $W$ without discarding any flat summand.

Relative to $S=V\oplus V\oplus W$, write $P=(B_1,B_2,J)^T$ and $Q=(Q_1,Q_2,Q_W)^T$. The coefficient of $\lambda_1\mu_1$ in $\beta\alpha=0$ is $Q^\dagger HR+T^\dagger HP=0$, so $Q_1=-B_2^\dagger$; the coefficient of $\lambda_1\mu_2$ is $Q^\dagger HT-R^\dagger HP=0$, so $Q_2=B_1^\dagger$. Define $I^\dagger=Q_W$. These definitions give exactly the displayed $\alpha$ and, by the lifted reality identity, the displayed $\beta$.

The $\lambda_1^2$ coefficient of $\beta\alpha=0$ is $Q^\dagger HP=0$. Substitution of the blocks gives $-[B_2,B_1]+IJ=[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. The $\lambda_1\lambda_2$ coefficient is $Q^\dagger HQ-P^\dagger HP=0$. Expanding it gives $[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J=0$, which is $\mu_{\mathbb R}=0$. Conversely, these two moment equations make all coefficients of $\beta\alpha$ vanish, and direct substitution yields $$\beta\alpha=\lambda_1^2\mu_{\mathbb C} +\lambda_1\lambda_2\mu_{\mathbb R} -\lambda_2^2\mu_{\mathbb C}^\dagger=0.$$

Let a normalized framed chain isomorphism have domain, middle and target maps $g_-,g_0,g_+$. It preserves $H$, so $g_0$ is unitary. Comparing the two $\mu$ coefficients forces $g_0|_{V\oplus0}=g_-$ and $g_0|_{0\oplus V}=g_-$; unitarity then preserves $W_0$. The infinity framing is fixed, so $g_0|_{W_0}=1$. Thus $g_0=\operatorname{diag}(g,g,1)$ for one $g\in U(V)$, and the $\lambda$ coefficients force $B_i'=gB_ig^{-1}$, $I'=gI$, and $J'=Jg^{-1}$. Surjectivity of $\beta$ makes $g_+$ uniquely determined and equal to $g$. Conversely, each such $g$ defines the displayed pairing-preserving framed chain isomorphism. Hence there are no residual transformations beyond simultaneous $U(V)$.

On the affine chart $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2] =[1:0:z_1:z_2]$, the raw maps are $a_z$ and $b_z^\dagger$ from [F5]. Since the original $\alpha,\beta$ have their required ranks at every point, [F5] gives costability and stability. Thus the extracted zero-moment datum is regular. Conversely, for stable and costable data, [F5] proves full homogeneous rank, composition zero, and local splitting, so the raw formula does define the required monad.

Put $B_1'=t_1B_1$, $B_2'=t_2B_2$, $I'=Ih^{-1}$, and $J'=t_1t_2hJ$. Substituting $(\lambda_1,t_1t_2\lambda_2,t_1\mu_1,t_2\mu_2)$ into the primed $A,C$ gives $A'=t_1A$ and $C'=t_2C$. Substitution into $\alpha'$ then gives $$\alpha'(g_tz)(t_1t_2)^{-1} =\operatorname{diag}(t_2^{-1},t_1^{-1},h)\alpha(z).$$ The same substitution into $\beta'$ gives $\beta'(g_tz)\operatorname{diag}(t_2^{-1},t_1^{-1},h)=\beta(z)$. The factors therefore are the stated chain maps; on the framed flavor coordinates $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_a^{-1})$ supplies the stated weights.

After lifting reduced orthonormal bases, the common Gram matrix of the two $\mu$ coefficient maps has the form $I+\epsilon K$ with $K=K^\dagger$. The change $T=I-\tfrac12\epsilon K$ satisfies $T^\dagger(I+\epsilon K)T=I$ using $\epsilon^2=0$ and $\bar\epsilon=\epsilon$. This normalizes both $\mu$ maps over $A$ without ordering nilpotent elements or asserting nilpotent positivity. Choices of lifted normalized bases differ by the residual $U(k,A)$ action proved in step 5.2, so coefficient extraction is independent of those choices on isomorphism classes.

For any such raw datum and finite $z$, write $a_z=(B_1-z_1,B_2-z_2,J)^T$ and $b_z^\dagger=(-B_2+z_2,B_1-z_1,I)$. The two moment equations give $b_z^\dagger a_z=0$ and $a_z^\dagger a_z=b_z^\dagger b_z=:f_z$. Regularity makes both maps full rank, so $f_z$ is positive definite. On $\ell_z$ the monad is $\alpha=a_z\lambda_1+b_z\lambda_2$ and $\beta=b_z^\dagger\lambda_1-a_z^\dagger\lambda_2$. The cross Gram terms vanish, and $a_z,b_z$ identify two orthogonal copies of $V$ after applying $f_z^{-1/2}$. In these orthonormal coordinates the end maps on the first two copies are $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)^T$ and $(-\lambda_2,\lambda_1)$, the Euler complex $V\mathcal O(-1)\to(V\oplus V)\mathcal O\to V\mathcal O(1)$; the complementary term is $E_z\mathcal O$. Hence $H^0(F|_{\ell_z})=E_z$ with its positive induced form, and $F|_{\ell_z}$ is trivial. At infinity the same calculation in step 4.1 gives $W\otimes\mathcal O$ and its framing. The maps in step 6.1 are exactly the required locally split end maps.

The zero-level quotient result [F8] applies because step 6.1 established stability and both zero moments; it identifies each regular complex orbit with its unique unitary orbit. The explicit argument in step 5.2 is stronger for the framed real monads: it identifies their actual normalized isomorphisms with $U(V)$ and fixes the inverse extraction orbit. If a constant flat summand is present, [F2] places it in the framed $W_0$ complement and the same fixed-frame argument leaves it unchanged. When $k=0$, every map into or out of $V=0$ is zero and $U(0)$ has one element. Because all coefficient images lie in $M=L^\perp$, $J$ has no component in the framed flat subspace $L\subset W$ and $I$ vanishes on that subspace. Thus flat directions remain as unused directions of $W$.

The coefficient equations in steps 4.2 and 5.1 are polynomial identities, so over $A$ they give the same block form and both moment equations. Conversely, take an $A$-valued zero-moment datum whose reduction is regular. Every full-rank minor of its reduced raw maps lifts to a unit in the local rings of the first-order thickening; thus the end maps are locally split and the cohomology is locally free. On a fixed real line the matrices $a_z,b_z$ have full-rank reductions, so their common Gram $f_z$ is invertible over $A$. Their orthogonal images split off two free copies of $V_A$, leaving a free rank-$N$ complement; the line complex is the Euler complex plus that constant complement, so its sections commute with reduction. The global section and coefficient-image conditions are exactly the additional range conditions imposed in the Statement. The standard middle form induces a nondegenerate real pairing, positive after reduction. Thus such data give families in the stated range. The proof of step 5.2 uses only coefficient comparison, the framing, and $g^\dagger g=1$, so it gives exactly $U(k,A)$ as the residual group. Reduction and each map $\epsilon\mapsto r\epsilon$ commute with coefficient extraction and with the correction $T$. This proves first-order naturality for precisely the stated base changes.

The finite monad resolution and its locally free cohomology give the algebraic Chern character and Chern classes in [F7]. Its same finite line resolution yields the topological classes after the hyperplane cycle class is identified with the Euler class of the complex normal line. The positive incidence-fiber Thom calculation in [F7] gives $\pi^*u=H_{\rm top}^2$. If the topological bundle is $\pi^*E$, naturality gives $\pi^*c_2(E)=kH_{\rm top}^2=k\pi^*u$; since $\pi^*u$ is a generator, $c_2(E)=ku$. This is conditional on the pullback hypothesis and asserts no Ward correspondence.
